source_refs.note: Basic Properties of Amides: a main subheading of 24.5 Amides, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 127-127.

blocks.text: Amides are less basic than aliphatic amines. Unlike amines, amides form neutral solutions in water. They exhibit resonance where the lone pair on nitrogen participates in delocalization with oxygen of carbonyl group. This reduces the availability of electrons on nitrogen, thereby decreasing the basicity.

blocks.alt: R-C(=O)-NH2 with a lone pair on N and two curly arrows (the C=O electrons move onto O; the N lone pair moves into the C-N bond), a double-headed resonance arrow, and R-C(-O-)=NH2+.
blocks.caption: Resonance in an amide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 128).

blocks.text: The introduction of double bond character between carbon and nitrogen reduces the C—N bond length less than the usual C—N single bond length.

blocks.alt: R-C(=O)-NH2 with an arrow to its C-N bond labelled (132 pm), and R-CH2-NH2 with an arrow to its C-N bond labelled (147 pm).
blocks.caption: C-N bond lengths in an amide and in an amine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 128).
